title: ELECTRA: A Cartesian Network for 3D Charge Density Prediction with Floating Orbitals

metadata.authors: J. Elsborg; L. Thiede; A. N. Aspuru-Guzik; T. Vegge; A. Bhowmik

source_summary: ELECTRA is an equivariant model that predicts electronic charge densities using floating Gaussian orbitals by data-driven placement and parameterization, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy and efficiency, and reducing DFT computation time by over 50% on unseen molecules.
abstract: We present the Electronic Tensor Reconstruction Algorithm (ELECTRA) - an equivariant model for predicting electronic charge densities using floating orbitals. Floating orbitals are a long-standing concept in the quantum chemistry community that promises more compact and accurate representations by placing orbitals freely in space, as opposed to centering all orbitals at the position of atoms. Finding the ideal placement of these orbitals requires extensive domain knowledge, though, which thus far has prevented widespread adoption. We solve this in a data-driven manner by training a Cartesian tensor network to predict the orbital positions along with orbital coefficients. This is made possible through a symmetry-breaking mechanism that is used to learn position displacements with lower symmetry than the input molecule while preserving the rotation equivariance of the charge density itself. Inspired by recent successes of Gaussian Splatting in representing densities in space, we are using Gaussian orbitals and predicting their weights and covariance matrices. Our method achieves a state-of-the-art balance between computational efficiency and predictive accuracy on established benchmarks. Furthermore, ELECTRA is able to lower the compute time required to arrive at converged DFT solutions - initializing calculations using our predicted densities yields an average 50.72 % reduction in self-consistent field (SCF) iterations on unseen molecules.

methods.value: Develop and train the Electronic Tensor Reconstruction Algorithm (ELECTRA), an equivariant model that predicts 3D charge density using floating Gaussian orbitals and a symmetry-breaking mechanism to learn position displacements.

problems.value: The long-standing challenge in quantum chemistry of efficiently and accurately representing electronic charge densities using floating orbitals without extensive domain knowledge.

hypotheses.value: A data-driven approach can predict the optimal placement of floating orbitals and their coefficients to reconstruct ground truth charge densities.

evidence.value: ELECTRA achieves state-of-the-art balance between computational efficiency and predictive accuracy on the QM9 dataset, reducing self-consistent field (SCF) iterations by 50.72% on unseen molecules.

conclusions.value: ELECTRA demonstrates a fully data-driven approach to charge density prediction that outperforms existing methods in accuracy and computational efficiency.

failure_paths.value: failure: Initial attempts with equivariant neural networks without symmetry-breaking showed constrained Gaussian positions due to input symmetry. Evidence: Outputs were constrained to the reflection plane, severely limiting the density constructed based on a Gaussian centered on the predicted locations.

success: Using symmetry-breaking inputs by initializing with the eigenvectors of the moment of inertia tensor for each atom. Evidence: The model could learn its own set of symmetry-breaking vectors, allowing output not constrained by the symmetry of the input molecule.
